_doc: The townspeople's own questions (topics.json format): about them, their work, their families and their Pokémon. Loaded through topics.json 'more'.

topics.label: Do you like running the inn?
topics.note: Mom loves Pallet House. She also gets tired. She never says so.

delia: I do, sweetie. The soup, the people, the view. Even Old Tom's stories, the third time.
Some evenings my feet ache like they've walked to Viridian and back. But I never actually go anywhere. Funny, isn't it?

topics.label: What's your favourite flower?
topics.note: Mom's favourite: Grandma's roses. And the sweet peas Rose gives her.

delia: Grandma's roses. Red, a little wild, and they come back every year no matter what I do to them.
A bit like someone I know.

topics.label: Why do you worry so much?
topics.ash: Mom... why do you worry so much?
topics.note: Mom worries because she loves him. She's working on it.

delia: Because you're my whole world, honey, and the world is very big, and you're going to walk right out into it.
I'm practising worrying less. I've got it down to four times a day. Mr. Mime keeps count.

topics.label: Did you ever leave Pallet?
topics.note: Mom has hardly ever left Pallet. She once had plans to.

lines: Viridian, for flour. Pewter once, for a wedding. That's it, really.
I had plans, once. Big ones. Then I had something better. You. And the inn, and the town...
N: (She straightens your cap, though it was already straight.)

topics.label: What should I pack?
topics.ash: What should I pack for my journey?
topics.note: Mom's packing list: socks. Many socks.

delia: Clean socks. Lots. A sweater. A first-aid kit. Rubber gloves, for the electric ones. More socks.
And something from home, sweetie. Something small. For the nights when it feels very far.

topics.label: Can you teach me to cook?
topics.note: Mom will teach him Grandma's stew. He's surprisingly good at it.

delia: Really? Oh, honey. Yes! Grandma's stew first. Then omelettes. Then you'll never go hungry on the road.
You've watched me do it your whole life. I bet you're better than you think.

topics.label: What's in the drawer in the hall?
topics.note: There's a drawer Mom doesn't talk about. Some things can wait.

delia: Hm? Oh, old things, sweetie. Papers. A photo or two. Nothing that needs looking at today.
Ask me again when you're older. Not much older. A little.

topics.label: How's Nibbles today?
topics.note: Nibbles: Lily's Caterpie. Loves soft leaves, hates being poked, listens to everything.

lily: He ate three leaves and a petal! The petal was an accident. He looked very surprised.
I told him about my whole morning. He fell asleep at the good part. I think that means he's relaxed.

topics.label: Why Butterfree?
topics.note: Lily loves Butterfree because they start small and end up flying.

lily: Because they start as the smallest, slowest thing, and they end up FLYING. Everybody laughs at Caterpie. Nobody laughs at Butterfree.

topics.label: What's your Master plan?
topics.note: Lily's plan: Nibbles first, then a Butterfree, then a team of Bug types, then everything.

lily: Step one, Butterfree. Step two, a Beedrill, but a nice one. Step three, beat you. Step four, beat everyone.
I wrote it down. It's on my wall. You're on it, as step three.

topics.label: Are you and Timmy friends?
topics.note: Lily and Timmy: rivals. Also friends. Don't tell them.

lily: NO. He's my RIVAL. We play tag every day and I win most of the time. ...He's okay. Don't tell him I said okay.

topics.label: What's your mom like?
topics.note: Rose, Lily's mum: slow, kind, knows every flower.

lily: She talks to flowers. Like, actually talks. And she knows when I'm sad before I do. It's really annoying. I love her.

topics.label: Why flowers?
topics.note: Rose grows flowers because they keep their promises.

rose: Because they keep their promises, Ash. Plant a bulb in autumn, and it comes up in spring. Not many things are that honest.

topics.label: Do flowers mean things?
topics.note: Flower meanings: sweet peas for goodbye, forget-me-nots for remember me, sunflowers for loyalty.

rose: Every one. Sweet peas mean goodbye and thank you. Forget-me-nots mean what they say. Sunflowers mean I'll follow you.
When you go, I'll give your mother sweet peas. And you forget-me-nots. Don't lose them.

topics.label: Do POKéMON like your garden?
topics.note: Oddish come to Rose's garden at dusk. Grass types like quiet and good soil.

rose: The Oddish do. They walk in at dusk and plant themselves in the bed by the gate. I leave it empty for them.
Grass POKéMON like what plants like. Good soil, sun, and not being stepped on.

topics.label: Is Mom your best friend?
topics.note: Rose and Mom have been best friends since they were girls.

rose: Since we were seven. She pulled me out of the duck pond. I've been following her around ever since. Well. She stopped going anywhere. So I stayed too.

topics.label: How do you make bread?
topics.note: Bread: flour, water, salt, yeast, time. Mostly time.

bram: Flour, water, salt, yeast, and time, lad! Mostly time! You can't hurry a dough. It knows. It sulks.

topics.label: Why get up at four?
topics.note: Bram gets up at four so the town has bread by six.

bram: Because the town wants bread at six, and bread wants four hours! HO HO! Also, the ovens are lonely without me.

topics.label: What's your best bread?
topics.note: Bram's best: honey rolls. His proudest: the rye, with a burnt corner.

bram: The honey rolls, as you well know, little thief! But my proudest is the rye. Dark, heavy, and a burnt corner for character!

topics.label: Is Ada really the boss?
topics.note: In the Hollis house, Ada is the boss. Everyone knows it.

bram: Ada? The boss? Of course she is! I bake the bread, she sells it, and Timmy eats it. That's a business, lad!

topics.label: How's the bread round?
topics.note: Ada's round: twelve houses, twelve loaves, twelve stories.

ada: Twelve houses, twelve loaves, twelve bits of news! You'd be amazed what people tell you at seven in the morning, dear.

topics.label: Do you ever get stories wrong?
topics.note: Ada never gets stories wrong. She improves them.

ada: Wrong? Never! I improve them, dear. A story's like bread. It's better with a little extra.

topics.label: How did you meet Bram?
topics.note: Ada met Bram when he dropped a tray of rolls at her feet. On purpose, he says.

ada: He dropped a whole tray of rolls at my feet at the Viridian fair! Said it was an accident. It was NOT an accident. Twenty years ago!

topics.label: Is Timmy always like this?
topics.note: Timmy: always like this.

ada: Like what, dear? Loud? Sticky? In love with you? Yes, yes and yes. Since he could walk.

topics.label: What's your favourite POKéMON?
topics.note: Timmy's favourite POKéMON: changes every day. Today, Gyarados.

timmy: GYARADOS! No, DRAGONITE! No, PIKACHU! ...What's a Pikachu do, again? I'll pick it anyway!

topics.label: What do you want to be?
topics.note: Timmy wants to be Ash's assistant. Then a Master.

timmy: Your ASSISTANT! I'll carry your bag and clean your badges! And then when you retire I'll be a Master too!

topics.label: Where's your secret base?
topics.note: Timmy's secret base: by the pond. It has a sign.

timmy: I can't TELL you! It's SECRET! ...It's by the pond. In the reeds. There's a sign that says SECRET BASE. Don't tell anyone.

topics.label: Is Grandpa's ladle story true?
topics.note: Timmy believes every one of Old Tom's stories. All of them.

timmy: YES! He fought a GYARADOS with a SPOON! It was a ladle. Same thing! He's the bravest grandpa in the world!

topics.label: Why do you feed the Pidgey?
topics.note: Mae feeds the Pidgey because her husband did. Forty years.

mae: My husband started it, dearie. Crusts on the step every morning. When he passed, the Pidgey kept coming. So I kept feeding them.
Now they're my company. Twenty-two of them. They don't talk back, which is restful.

topics.label: Got any old sayings?
topics.note: Mae's sayings: you can't hold a river in a teacup.

mae: Plenty, dearie. 'You can't hold a river in a teacup.' 'A Slowpoke still gets there.' 'Never trust a Meowth with your purse.'
That last one's practical, not wise.

topics.label: What was your husband like?
topics.note: Mae's husband: a fisherman. Kind, slow, sang badly. Took her to the Cinnabar springs.

mae: A fisherman, dearie. Slow and kind, like an old boat. Sang terribly. Took me to the Cinnabar springs for our honeymoon.
I still have the pebble he gave me there. It's warm, somehow. Always.

topics.label: What are you knitting?
topics.note: Mae is always knitting something for someone.

mae: Socks for Gus, who won't wear them, a hat for Timmy, who'll lose it, and something for you, which is a secret.
Knitting is just worrying with your hands, dearie. Your mother should take it up.

topics.label: What's a PC?
topics.note: Kai has the only PC in town. It stores things. And plays music.

kai: A Personal Computer, kiddo! You can store things on it! Letters, pictures, recipes! Some trainers even store POKéMON in them! How? Nobody knows!

topics.label: How does the radio work?
topics.note: Kai's radio: talks to boats as far as Seafoam.

kai: Waves in the air, invisible, faster than a Pidgeot! I talk into this, a boat off Seafoam hears it! INCREDIBLE!

topics.label: Do you and Gus really bet?
topics.note: Kai and Gus bet on the weather. Gus is winning, 41 to 39.

kai: Every day! Radio versus clouds! He's winning forty-one to thirty-nine, but my radio's had a NEW AERIAL since Tuesday.

topics.label: Biggest fish you ever caught?
topics.note: Kai's biggest catch: a Seaking. Or a boot.

kai: A Seaking, kiddo! THIS big! It got away. But it was this big. Marina says it was a boot. Marina's wrong.

topics.label: How do you mend a net?
topics.note: Mending nets: patient knots, good twine, one hole at a time.

marina: One hole at a time. Square knots, tight, good twine. Rush it and the fish walk right out. Like most things.

topics.label: Is Kai always like that?
topics.note: Kai: always like that. Marina married him anyway.

marina: Always. Woke me at three to listen to static once. Said it was a whale. Thirteen years. I'd marry him again. Don't tell him.

topics.label: What's the best fish?
topics.note: Best fish: whatever came in this morning.

marina: Whatever came in this morning. Fresh beats fancy. Your mum takes the mackerel on Fridays. Good woman.

topics.label: Why are you so tough?
topics.note: Marina is tough because the sea is.

marina: Because the sea doesn't care if you're nice. You have to care for yourself. Then you can afford to be nice. Underneath.

topics.label: Does Doduo have a name?
topics.note: Ben's Doduo has two names. One per head.

ben: Two. Left's Dot. Right's Duncan. Mm. They don't answer to either.

topics.label: What do you grow?
topics.note: Ben grows wheat, berries and beans. Bram buys the wheat.

ben: Wheat for Bram. Berries for Mae's birds, whatever she says. Beans for me. Mm. And weeds for Rose to complain about.

topics.label: Why do you always say 'Mm'?
topics.note: Ben says 'Mm' because it covers most things.

topics.label: Sorry about the wheat.
topics.ash: Sorry I flattened your wheat. Chasing that Nidoran.
topics.note: Ben forgave the wheat. Things grow back.

topics.label: Were you really a sailor?
topics.note: Old Tom sailed forty years, round Kanto twice.

tom: Forty years, lad! Round Kanto twice, and halfway to Johto once, before the cook mutinied over the soup.

topics.label: Tell me a sea story!
topics.note: Old Tom's stories: half are true. He won't say which half.

tom: Once, off Seafoam, the fog came down so thick we navigated by the sound of Seel clapping. Clap to port, clap to starboard.
Got home safe. Owe those Seel a fish to this day.

topics.label: What do you watch with the spyglass?
topics.note: Old Tom watches Cinnabar, the boats, and Gus.

tom: Cinnabar, lad. The boats. And Gus, up his tower, to see if he's asleep. He never is. It's very annoying.

topics.label: Who was the best Trainer you met?
topics.note: The best Trainer Tom met talked to his Butterfree every night.

tom: A quiet fellow with a Butterfree. Never won a thing. Talked to it every night on deck. When we hit a storm it flew ahead and found us the channel.
That's a Master, lad. Not the trophies. The trust.

topics.label: What's in the logbook?
topics.note: Gus's logbook: every ship, storm, shake and Pidgey for forty years.

gus: Ships. Storms. Shakes. Pidgey. The time and the wind and anything that isn't usual. Forty years of usual, and the odd unusual.

topics.label: How does the lamp work?
topics.note: The lighthouse lamp: a big lens, a small flame, turned every night.

gus: A small flame and a big lens. The lens does the work. I just keep it clean and keep it turning. Most important jobs are like that.

topics.label: Why be a lighthouse keeper?
topics.note: Gus became a keeper so that everyone gets home.

gus: So that everyone gets home, Ash. That's the whole reason. Four boats out, four boats home.

topics.label: What do you do all night?
topics.note: At night Gus watches, logs, and listens.

gus: Watch. Log. Listen. Drink tea. Watch some more. It sounds dull. It's the best part of my day.

topics.label: Seen anything strange?
topics.note: Gus has seen strange lights at sea. He logs what he sees, not what he thinks.

gus: A boat without lights, some nights. A glow under the water off the point. I log what I see, Ash. What it was is someone else's job.

topics.label: What's your favourite POKéMON?
topics.note: Prof. Oak's favourite: whichever he's studying.

oak: Whichever one I'm studying that day, Ash! Today, Doduo. Two heads, one body. Do they argue? Do they agree? Fascinating!

topics.label: Were you a Trainer?
topics.note: Prof. Oak was a Trainer once. A good one, he admits.

oak: Once upon a time. I was rather good, if I say so myself. And I do. Then I realised I wanted to know POKéMON more than I wanted to beat them.

topics.label: What's the hardest part of a journey?
topics.note: The hardest part of a journey, Oak says: losing, and coming back from it.

oak: Losing, my boy. Not the losing itself. Getting up afterwards, and asking yourself honestly why.
The Trainers who learn from losing go furthest. Every single time.

topics.label: Why do Trainers start at ten?
topics.note: Trainers start at ten in Kanto: old enough to care for something, young enough to learn.

oak: Old enough to look after something, young enough to learn from it. That's the theory. Some ten-year-olds prove it right, some wrong.

topics.label: What should a Trainer carry?
topics.note: Oak's list: Potions, POKé BALLS, a map, food for two, and a way to call home.

oak: Potions, POKé BALLS, a map. Food for two, because your partner eats too. And a way to call home, Ash. Use it.

topics.label: Do POKéMON dream?
topics.note: Do POKéMON dream? Oak thinks so. They twitch.

oak: I believe they do. Watch a sleeping Growlithe sometime. Its paws run. Its tail wags. Wherever it is, it's having a lovely time.

topics.label: Is it far to Viridian?
topics.note: Viridian is a few hours' walk up Route 1 from the tea stop.

tea_keeper: A few hours more, young one, if you don't stop to chase every Pidgey. You will, of course. Everyone does.

topics.label: What tea do you make?
topics.note: The tea stop on Route 1: green tea from Hana's own bushes.

tea_keeper: Green tea from my own bushes, with spring water from up the hill. On the house for anyone starting a journey, dear.

topics.label: What do you sell?
topics.note: The POKé MART: Potions, POKé BALLS, Antidotes, Repels.

mart_clerk: Potions, POKé BALLS, Antidotes, Repels! Everything a new Trainer needs. Except confidence. We're sold out of that.

topics.label: Any tips for a new Trainer?
topics.note: The clerk's tip: always carry one more Potion than you think.

mart_clerk: Always carry one more Potion than you think you'll need. And read the labels. You'd be amazed.
